paper_id: Han and Liu - 2006 - Dubious feedback fair or not
title: Dubious Feedback: Fair or Not?
motivation: P2P reputation systems suffer from malicious feedback that defames trustworthy peers or overpraises group members, but no mechanism validates feedback quality
problem_framing: Define feedback validation problem by measuring feedback deviation via Feedback Valid Degree (FVD) and integrating it into reputation computation
key_insight: A peer's own reputation should be impacted by the quality of feedback it provides about others, creating an incentive for honest evaluation
method_signature: TruthRep uses super-peer architecture with consultants and PID controller to incorporate feedback quality into reputation scoring
evaluation_criteria: Reputation degradation of malicious peers and reputation computation error compared to conventional approach
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Precise validation parameter computation is computationally infeasible in large P2P systems; real-time reputation reporting remains challenging
evidence_for_taste: The lack of authentication makes it difficult to differentiate
the precision of deciding on feedback credibility is still a challenging issue

thinking_moves: Identify three attack vectors for reputation tampering then systematize feedback components

Criticize existing work for lacking protection from clique cheating and not combining incentive with feedback quality
